answer: Each agent keeps a registered sparrow with unique feather patterns. Each epoch, the agent plucks one feather, dips it in the epoch pigment and presses the ledger. The page floats on a pond; the press sends ripple rings out, and cameras time them to the edge, proving it happened live. A feather regrows in 14 days, so one sparrow covers 26 presses a year. Faking 1,000 agents costs $180,000 in trained sparrows ($180 each) plus 1,000 pigment batches and 1,000 live presses in a day. Like a postmark: a thousand feathers must press one page, and one dry feather gives the forgery away.
